 The Honourable Smt Justice V.Sujatha
 Writ Petition No: 17797/2024
Between:

 And

Counsel for the Petitioner(S):
 1. M Venkata Ramana Reddy

 1. Gp For Roads Buildings

2. Gp For Muncipal Admn Urban Dev
 3. Gp For Revenue

The Court made the following:
 Order:

This Writ Petition came to be filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India seeking the following relief:-
"....to issue a writ or direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the action of the respondents more particularly respondents No.2 to 5 in trying to demolish the buildings of the petitioners bearing Door No.7/1385 AND 7/1386 Korrapadu Road, Revenue Ward No.7 Proddatur 516360 YSR Kadapa District without issuing notice and without following due process of law or without acquiring proceedings under the Provisions of Right to Fair Compensation Bachu Venkata Subbaraja Gupta vs The State Of Ap on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31507310/
1 and Transparency in land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 is as illegal, arbitrary, unconstitutional and contrary to the provisions laid down in the Act and violative of Article 300A of Constitution Act

sentences.text: and consequently direct the respondents not to demolish the petitioners building property bearing Door No.7/1382 AND 7/1383 Korrapadu Road, Revenue Ward No.7 Proddatur, 516360 YSR Kadapa District without issuing notice and pass...."

2. The petitioner Nos.1, 2 who are brothers and one Munaga Narasimhulu purchased a house with varanda in Door Nos.7/1382 and 7/1383 situated in Korrapadu Road, Prdddatur Town admeasuring to an extent of 54.71 square yards and 23.72 square yards from one Chakali Gurumurthy vide document No.2113/2014 dated 11.04.2014.

The 3rd petitioner herein purchased a house along with veranda in Door Nos.7/1382 and 7/1383 situated in Korrapadu Road, Proddatur Town admeasuring an extent of 54.71 square yards and 17.74 square yards from one Chakali Gurumurthy vide document No.2112/2014, dated 11.04.2014.
Since then, the petitioners have been in possession of the subject property.

3. While so, the 4th respondent authorities have visited the subject property and started to make markings on the petitioners' scheduled property and on questioning, the petitioners were informed that the respondents need to acquire 40 feet of land on both sides for widening of Korrapdu road from 60 feet to 100 feet.
As the aforesaid action of the respondents is without issuing any notice and without following due process of law, the present writ petition is filed.

4. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned Government Pleader for Roads and Buildings.
5.

Today when the writ petition came up for hearing, learned Government Pleader has produced a copy of instructions of the 5th respondent vide Ref.No.A/355/2024, dated 12.08.2024, wherein it is stated that the process of acquisition of land for the purpose of widening of the existing road was not initiated and no requisition was received from the Municipal Commissioner, Proddatur for acquisition of land.

It is further stated that at present, the structure of the petitioners property situated in D.Nos.7/1382 and 7/1383, Korrapadu Road, Revenue Ward No.7, Proddatur town and mandal was not acquired for the purpose of widening of the existing road from 60 feet to 100 feet.

6. As per the instructions of the 5th respondent, it is clear that the Revenue Department has not received any acquisition from the Municipal Commissioner i.e. the 4th respondent herein for widening of the existing road from 60 feet to 100 feet in Korrapadu Road, Revenue ward No.7,
Proddatur Town.

7. In view of the above, instead of keeping the writ petition pending, this Court feels it appropriate to dispose of the writ petition by directing the respondent Nos. 2 to 5 not to interfere with the possession of the petitioners' property bearing in D.Nos.7/1382 and 7/1383, Korrapadu road,
revenue ward No.7 of Proddatur Town and Mandal, without following due process of law.
As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
